entry.summary: Tienes una señal que a cada observación te dice en qué estado estás: un monitor de salud que dice OK o CAÍDO, un detector de conectividad, un clasificador de modo. Y cerca del umbral oscila: OK, CAÍDO, OK, CAÍDO, OK. Cada cambio dispara algo —una alerta, un failover, entrar o salir de una posición— y de repente tu sistema está temblando por ruido, no por una transición real. Es el mismo problema que resuelve el termostato de tu casa desde hace un siglo, y la solución tiene nombre: histéresis. No cambies de estado hasta que el nuevo se haya sostenido. entry.title: My most profitable actor was silently failing most of its runs. The bug was one unprotected line.
entry.summary: My oldest actor is also my most profitable one - it's caught more paying clients than anything else I've shipped. Which made it worse when I found out it had been silently failing on a large share of its runs, for a while, and I only caught it by accident. The actor watches CBOE options data on a schedule and flags contracts trading at volumes far above their normal baseline - the kind of activity that sometimes precedes real news. Every step of the actual detection logic was already wrapped in error handling. Except one: the very last line, the one that sends the results out. That line, Actor.push_data(results), had no try/except around it. If a single row in the batch was malformed - one bad character, one field that didn't serialize cleanly - the whole call could fail, and with it the entire run, even though every ticker had already been checked correctly. All that work, thrown away by one line at the very end. Apify doesn't show actor owners the logs of runs triggered by clients, only your own test runs. So this had been failing quietly, on other people's schedules, with no way for me to see why - just a success rate that didn't look right. The fix: wrap the push in a fallback - try the whole batch first, and only if that fails, retry row by row so one bad row gets dropped instead of taking the rest down with it. Only raise for real if literally nothing could be sent. Tested against a forced bulk failure, a single bad row, and a total outage before shipping it - each one now behaves the way it's supposed to. I also added a last-resort email alert: if a run ever fails end to end now, for any reason, I get a message instead of finding out weeks later from a success-rate graph. https://apify.com/0xgollum/unusual-options-activity

entry.title: This is NOVEL
entry.summary: I am excited to share a project I have been developing: an edgeless, decoupled WordPress architecture built specifically for modern newsrooms. By utilizing WordPress with SQLite and a decoupled Next.js frontend and backend, I have rebuilt the platform to eliminate traditional backend limitations while preserving all core functionality. Key features of this custom build include: Media & Content Optimization: Automated HLS video conversion with AI-generated chapters and captions, choice of AI voice transcriptions for articles, automated photo optimization, and cryptographic digital watermarking. Advanced Analytics & Data: Full integration with ClickHouse via Apache Lighthouse, a vector database for internal LLM use, built-in newsletter management, and telemetry. Infrastructure & Security: Unlimited horizontal scaling with a usage-based pricing model, edgeless SSO, an MCP server, and real-time machine learning-driven edge network hardening. Multi-Platform Distribution: Automated generation of React-based PWAs and native iOS/Android apps, alongside integrations with Apple News, Google News, video RSS, and automated YouTube syndication. Monetization & Engagement: Built-in A/B testing for articles and tools to create a programmatic ad network for independent monetization control.
